summary: Esben Andreasen works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and served as a visiting researcher at Otani University in 1992.
Esei Sasaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts as an associate professor at Ikenobo Junior College (attested 1979) and professor at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1991).

Eshin Nishimura (born 1933) is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Hanazono University, under Zenkei Shibayama, at Pendle Hill, and at Kyoto University (PhD). He later served as president of Hanazono University (2002–2005).
Esho Kawasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies who served as director at Bukkyo University (attested 1999) and president of Kyushu Ryukoku Gakkai (attested 2002).

Esho Mikogami (1935–2018) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who founded Indogaku Chibettogaku Kenkyū. He served as professor at Ryukoku University until 2003 and was president of the Ryukoku Buddhist Society in 1997.

Esho Yamaguchi (1918–2005) was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1939–1942) and held professorships at Osaka University (~1968–1982) and Ritsumeikan University (~1982–1989).
Eshun Otsuka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a research student at Taisho University, where he also held a post as a research student (attested 2013).

Ester Bianchi (born 1971) specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned PhDs at Ca' Foscari University and EPHE under Alfredo Cadonna and Jean-Noël Robert, and became Associate Professor at the University of Perugia around 2015.
Ethan Tischler specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Wesleyan University, completing his BA under the advisement of Mary-Jane Rubenstein (attested 2014).
Etienne Vermeersch (1934–2019) was a philosopher who studied at Ghent University from around 1953 to 1965. He subsequently held a post at Ghent University from 1967 to 1997.
Etsuaki Teraishi specializes in Indology and philosophy. He held posts as an associate professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and as a JSPS special researcher (attested 2001).

Eugen Hultzsch (1857–1927) was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig and Vienna under Georg Bühler. He served as Government Epigraphist in Madras (1886–1903) and held the chair of Sanskrit at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1903–1925).

Eugen Pander (1854–1894) specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. He studied at Polytechnikum Riga and in 1881 was appointed professor of economics and lecturer in Russian and German at Tongwen Guan.
Eugen Prym (1843–1913) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Bonn from around 1862 to 1867 and held an academic post there from approximately 1869 until 1913.

Eugen Wilhelm (1842–1923) was an Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies scholar who studied under August Schleicher. He served as a professor at the University of Jena from around 1869 to 1923.

Eugene Obermiller (1901–1935) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (~1921–1925). From around 1930 to 1935, he served at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Eugene Watson Burlingame (1876–1932) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Charles Rockwell Lanman. He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania, Johns Hopkins University (~1908–1913), and Yale University (~1917–1932).

Eugene Y. Wang specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied under Hung Wu and John M. Rosenfield, worked at the University of Chicago, and became Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Professor of Asian Art at Harvard University around 2005.
Eugenio d'Ors (1881–1954) was a Spanish philosopher who studied at the University of Barcelona (~1897–1903) and Universidad Central (~1903–1905), where he later held an academic post.
Eugenius Marius Uhlenbeck (1913–2003) was a linguist who studied at Leiden University from around 1932 to 1949. He served as a professor at Leiden University from 1950 to 1983, succeeding C. C. Berg.
